title.narrative: Output 6.2. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to strengthen policies and strategies to promote and ensure equal opportunities, participation and treatment between women and men, including equal remuneration for work of equal value

description.narrative:
In April 2021, 2 Ministerial Decrees (44 and 43) were issued by the Minister of Manpower (in coordination with the National Council for Women), removing restrictions on women's ability to work at night as well as giving them a choice to work in any institution or facility in any type, while providing all the necessary safety measures for protecting women at work, such as safe transportation and healthcare. The 2 new decrees were an update to the Ministerial Decrees (No 155 and 183) of 2003 issued by the Egyptian Minister of Manpower pursuant to the Labour Code and prohibited, respectively, women work in certain professions and women work at night in industries.
Pursuant to the Decree No 43 , the list of professions prohibited for women was limited to mines and quarries, which is a substantial progress compared to the list on the Decree No 155 of 2003. In addition, Article 3 of the same Decree (43) reduces prohibition of women's work in occupations and circumstances that involve risks and hazards to situations that pose harm to their reproductive health or the health of their children or fetuses during pregnancy and breast-feeding periods, legally prescribed by the Law. This follows up on a Direct Request addressed to Egypt by the CEACR in 2016 under Convention. 111. Decree No 44 allows women work in night shift in industries which pave the way for more opportunities for women in the industrial sector. The ILO, through its Gender DC portfolio, the Decent Work for Women in Egypt and Tunisia, the Gender-responsive Workplaces in Egypt and the Joint Programme for Decent and Productive Employment for Women in Egypt, Jordan and Palestine, has been supporting the Ministry of Manpower Gender and Non-Discrimination Unit (GU) in its efforts in operationalizing and institutionalizing its programmes. In the framework of the GU workplan, capacity building activities were organized during the reporting period for the GU members at the central and the local levels in order to increase their knowledge on gender equality, decent work and international labour standards and skills related to gender mainstreaming, planning and M& E. During these activities, continuous discussions took place comparing the national legislation including the labour code and Ministerial decrees to the provisions of the ILO gender conventions, particularly C. 100 (equal pay for equal work) and C. 111 (Discrimination) in employment and occupation. Also the ILO supported the GU efforts by conducting Participatory Gender Audit (PGA) for the Ministry (started September 2020). News about the trainings and its outcomes are available on the Ministry of Manpower Facebook Page: https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=1039062576517629&id=195780944179134

description.narrative: In June 2021, Egypt's National Wages Council (NWC), headed by Minister of Planning and Economic Development, has set the minimum wage for private sector workers at EGP 2,400 ($153) per month. The new ruling takes into account the economic conditions of the establishments that are currently unable to comply, and their exception to that, starting from 1 January 2022. The decision for minimum wage took into account several considerations. Foremost of these is the interest of workers and the need to achieve an appropriate increase in wages, whilst taking into account the current global economic conditions due to COVID-19 pandemic. It also takes into account the need to reduce the burdens on economic establishments to be able to continue their economic activities efficiently, as well as continue to perform their duties towards their employees. Hence, this decision is expected to support offset the negative effects of COVID 19 as well as increase productivity. In July 2020, the ILO has provided technical support on minimum wages through an online training workshop on the conception of Sustainable Minimum Wage Policies, which was carried out in support of the members of the National council for wages. The training contributed to enhance the capacity of the tripartite members of the council to understand, design, implement and enforce effective and coherent wage policies from a decent work perspective. In addition, to improve the evidence-base for wage setting, technical support was provided to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS, national institute of statistics under the umbrella of the MoPED) for the improvement of the data collection on wages, and specifically through a capacity building workshop implemented in March 2020 aiming at improving the regular Egyptian "Establishment Survey of Employment, wage and hours of work". With the Economic Research Forum (ERF), the ILO also recently collected data to monitor the evolution of labour market outcomes –employment and wages- during the Covid-19 crisis, and disseminated the related results. The technical support provided by the ILO to the National Council for Wages and to CAPMAS built on previous capacity building activities on minimum wages targeting the Egyptian constituents over several years. In support of its inputs into the policy dialogue on wages in Egypt and elsewhere in Africa, the ILO developed a Policy brief on wages in Africa. The national minimum wage is expected to contribute significantly to the reduction of the gender pay gap, given its importance at the bottom of the wage distribution: in Egypt in 2018 at the lowest decile of the wage distribution, female wage employees earned on average 32% less than their male counterparts (cf Wages in Africa, ILO, 2019).
